problem: Zero-shot VLM-LLM navigation pipelines pick 3D perception models by standalone pixel-level accuracy, with little study of how much perception quality is actually needed for a target navigation success rate under compute and latency limits.
motivation: Navigation is a multi-module system with limited compute and latency budgets, so perception should be judged by its contribution to downstream success (a Pareto view), not by standalone accuracy. The paper estimates empirical SR ceilings under controlled perception degradation to find where returns saturate.
key_idea: Quantify perception requirements of a slow-fast VLM-LLM navigator (SFCo-Nav) by controlled degradation (missed detections for the slow LLM planner, bounding-box center drift at target IoU for the fast reactive navigator) to derive empirical SR upper bounds, then validate them with ESAM variants.
insight: SR saturates quickly: with ideal perception, SR is about 41% at retention 0.20 and only 44.3% at 0.80, and SR stays around 33% for any box IoU above 0. The map from retention to matching score is roughly linear, while matching score to SR saturates. ESAM results stay below the bounds; the gap is attributed to false positives (which mislead the LLM) and distorted box aspect ratios (which break the Through Skill heading). A 20-class vocabulary performs about as well as a 200-class one. These attributions are argued in the text, not isolated by a dedicated ablation.
method: Ideal observation setup: for each viewpoint, a fixed-order sequence of GT objects (instruction-mentioned and scene-informative) with ideal boxes and correct labels serves as perfect perception.

Missed-detection simulation (slow planner): keep the first K = round(rho_ret*N) objects, so retained sets are nested; SFCo-Nav's slow brain builds a temporal-object bipartite topological graph from them.

Graph matching score: S_match = lambda*S_edge + (1-lambda)*S_obj, computed from object-name recall and (time, object) edge recall of the degraded graph vs the ideal graph, with lambda = 0.5. SR is analysed in three stages: rho vs SR, rho vs S_match, S_match vs SR.
Bounding-box drift (fast navigator): translate the box centroid by a random ±1-per-axis direction, scaled so IoU with the ideal box equals phi_iou; size and rotation are unchanged.

Geometry-aware skills: Approach (stop at c_noise minus u*(r_coll+delta_safe)) and Through (follow the normal of the minimal box dimension, p = c + sgn(u·n)·n·(0.5 s_j + delta_pass)); the target is projected to the nearest navigable viewpoint.

ESAM validation: Embodied SAM variants (partially trained on ScanNet200, plus the released 20-class model) run in Habitat with 40 frames per 360° rotation. AP@25 is the proxy for rho_ret and instance-level 3D box IoU is the proxy for phi_iou.

setting.backbone: GPT-4o (frozen) as SFCo-Nav slow brain; ESAM (SAM-based 3D instance segmentation) as perception in the validation
setting.training_data: none for the navigator (training-free); ESAM variants trained on ScanNet200 with different iteration budgets (300 to 118.63k)
setting.observation: Simulated ideal semantic observations with GT boxes; for the ESAM validation, 40 RGB-D frames per 360° rotation at each viewpoint
setting.action_space: discrete navigation-graph viewpoints, chosen from geometry-derived target points
setting.privileged: GT objects and boxes are used as the ideal observation in the simulation experiments; none for the ESAM runs

numbers_note: This is an analysis paper, not a leaderboard comparison; results are curves of SR vs perception level. The ESAM rows in the tables are ordered by increasing perception metric, but the text says the 20-class model gives 23.4 in the fast-navigator table, which does not match the row order (0.063 is the smallest IoU). The R2R split is not stated. Only the extreme rows are listed here; other rows are in the tables.
results: With ideal perception, slow-planner SR rises only from 41.0 to 44.3 as rho_ret goes from 0.20 to 0.80, and fast-navigator SR stays about 31-36% across all IoU levels. ESAM variants stay below these bounds (SR 30.2-33.7 for the planner, 23.4-26.4 for the navigator).
limitations: The simulation models only false negatives and centroid translation. It ignores false positives, scale and orientation errors, and the bounds are empirical, not proven.
Small evaluation sets (about 300-600 R2R instructions) and a single framework (SFCo-Nav) with GPT-4o, in discrete viewpoint navigation, so the conclusions may not generalize.
The results are noisy: SR fluctuates by several points across IoU levels, attributed to LLM instability.
